title: A Century of Schrödinger Equation (1926–2026): Recovering the Wave Picture and Its Physical Intuition
content: Schrödinger’s wave mechanics, developed in a series of papers published one century ago, offered an exceptionally intuitive route into the new atomic physics. The later axiomatic formulation of quantum mechanics brought indispensable mathematical precision, but it can also conceal the physical images that guided the original discovery. We revisit the optical–mechanical analogy behind Schrödinger’s construction and use it as a visual guide to stationary states, superposition, field modes, and gauge interactions. The analogies are deliberately heuristic and their limitations are stated: a quantum wavefunction is not, in general, a classical wave in ordinary space, and discrete classical modes do not by themselves imply quantized energy. Nevertheless, the wave viewpoint makes it possible to see the operator language of first and second quantization as the compact algebraic expression of an underlying mode structure. The purpose of this article is therefore not to replace the modern formalism, but to recover the physical intuition that makes that formalism intelligible.
